question: What will be the percentage change in front-month copper futures (HG=F on Yahoo Finance) from the close on 2026-08-21 to the close on 2026-09-27?
resolution_criteria: Resolves to 100 x (close on 2026-09-27 / close on 2026-08-21 - 1), using daily closes of HG=F on Yahoo Finance. If there is no close on 2026-09-27, the last close before it is used.

from the empirical distribution of 25-observation returns over the last 3 years (last year weighted double):

research:
Copper closed at about $6.58/lb on Friday 2026-08-21, which is the base for this question. Nothing has settled the outcome yet.

## 1. Resolution source
- I could not load the Yahoo Finance HG=F history page; the proxy refused the connection. Nothing below has been checked against Yahoo itself.
- 2026-08-21: Scrapmonster's COMEX copper table shows **$6.58/lb** for that day and $6.492 on 08-20. Gold Price Tracker also lists $6.58 for 08-21. Both are rounded to two decimals, so Yahoo's exact figure may differ slightly. [Scrapmonster](https://www.scrapmonster.com/comex/copper-price/353/9), [Gold Price Tracker](https://goldpricetracker.com/copper-history/2026-08/)
- Contract roll risk: HG=F currently follows the September 2026 contract. Under CME rules, my estimate is that September copper's last trading day falls around 2026-09-28. Yahoo may switch HG=F to December before 09-25, so any gap between the September and December prices could move the figure on its own. I did not confirm when Yahoo makes that switch.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has happened that settles or nearly settles the question. Prices sit just below record levels, and the main driver, the US decision on tariffs for refined copper, is still open.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- Week ending 2026-08-21: LPL's weekly recap says copper edged lower while gold and silver rose. [LPL](https://www.lpl.com/research/blog/weekly-market-performance-august-21-2026.html)
- Around 2026-08-20: Mining.com says copper touched record highs in three of four sessions, then fell back on profit-taking before Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech on Friday. LME official cash hit $14,525/t on Wednesday and three-month settled at $14,336. [Mining.com](https://www.mining.com/copper-price-extends-retreat-from-record-as-china-tests-the-tariff-trade/)
- 2026-08-17: LME copper reached about $14,396/t, its highest since late January. [Mining.com](https://www.mining.com/copper-price-sets-fresh-record-as-us-tariff-threat-wipes-out-global-surplus/)
- 2026-08-14: Based on the COMEX premium over LME, one analysis put the chance that the 15% refined-copper tariff starts on schedule at only about 14.6%. [Crux Investor](https://www.cruxinvestor.com/posts/us-copper-imports-hit-12-year-high-cutting-lme-stocks-14-raising-delivery-premiums)
- 2026-08-12/13: COMEX September copper set a record near $6.714/lb, then fell below $6.55 the next day on tariff uncertainty. The earlier record was $6.7045 on 08-05. LME stocks fell 14% to 214,550 t as metal moved into the US, and COMEX stocks hit a record. Crux Investor is a low-quality source. [Crux Investor](https://www.cruxinvestor.com/posts/us-copper-imports-hit-12-year-high-cutting-lme-stocks-14-raising-delivery-premiums), [Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/international-trade/us-copper-trades-near-record-on-tariff-risks-hormuz-speculation)
- 2026-08-06: Congo's ban on exports of copper and cobalt concentrate, in effect since 06-29, was made public and briefly lifted LME prices.
- 2026-06-30: This was Commerce's deadline to update the President on copper markets. The plan on the table is a phased tariff on refined copper: 15% in 2027 and 30% in 2028. One source says Commerce missed the deadline, and I found no confirmed final decision. [CRS](https://www.congress.gov/crs-product/IN12614), [Thompson Hine](https://www.thompsonhinesmartrade.com/2026/04/president-trump-makes-major-changes-to-section-232-tariffs-on-aluminum-steel-and-copper/), [C.H. Robinson](https://www.chrobinson.com/en-us/resources/insights-and-advisories/client-advisories/2026q2/06-02-2026-client-advisory-updates-to-section-232-tariffs-on-steel-aluminum-copper/)

## 4. Base rates
- August 2026 so far: COMEX traded roughly between $6.41 and $6.75, close to all-time highs. The 08-21 close is about 2% below the 08-12 record.
- This window is about 25 trading days. My own rough estimate, not from a source: if annualized volatility is 22-30%, a typical one-standard-deviation move over the window is about ±7-9%. Moves of ±15% or more over five weeks are uncommon but have happened around tariff news. In July 2025, COMEX copper fell about 20% in a single day when refined copper was left out of the tariffs.
- Asymmetric risk: because COMEX trades at a premium to LME (roughly $500/t in reports), news that lowers or delays the refined-copper tariff could shrink that premium and cut the price sharply. Confirmation of the tariff could push it higher.
- I could not get a verified series of past 5-week HG=F returns.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no prediction-market prices for copper on or near 2026-09-25 published by 2026-08-23. Kalshi does run daily and weekly copper markets (series KXCOPPERD / KXCOPPERW). [Kalshi](https://kalshi.com/markets/kxcopperw/copper-weekly-price/kxcopperw-26sep2517)
- 30rates.com published a model projection of about $6.31 for 08-21, below the actual price, so its record is weak. [30rates](https://30rates.com/copper)
- Bank forecasts: J.P. Morgan has a metals outlook page and Mining.com reports banks raising 2026 forecasts while warning the tariff premium could "collapse." I did not get specific September targets. [J.P. Morgan](https://www.jpmorgan.com/insights/global-research/commodities/aluminum-steel-copper-prices), [Mining.com](https://www.mining.com/copper-price-forecasts-lifted-for-2026-but-tariff-collapse-still-on-the-table/)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Any White House or Commerce announcement on refined-copper tariffs. This is the biggest swing factor for the COMEX premium.
- Market reaction on 08-24 to Warsh's Jackson Hole speech of 08-21, plus US payrolls (around 09-04), CPI (mid-September) and the FOMC meeting (around 09-15/16).
- China data: August PMIs (08-31 and 09-01) and activity and trade data in mid-September.
- Supply: how long Congo's concentrate export ban lasts, plus disruptions at Chilean and Peruvian mines.
- Inventories: changes in LME, COMEX and Shanghai stocks and the LME cash-to-three-month spread.
- The September contract nearing expiry, first notice day around 08-31, and Yahoo's possible switch of HG=F to December before 09-25.
